messages:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT detected — elevated egress failure rate for Private VPC peering from westeurope (region) to on‑prem circuits. Alert: https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/INC-1750001234 :red_circle:
Maya: I'm paged, investigating. Starting an incident thread here. P1 for private customers. @Jonas can you own the network side? I'll own customer comms and app-side checks.
Jonas: taking network lead. pulling BGP and route tables now.
Jonas: quick grep of BGP sessions to onprem-router-01: seeing intermittent withdraws. last flaps at ~1750001100 -> 1750001180.
Jonas: here are the peer statuses from our router vty:
```
peer 10.20.30.1   AS 65010  state: Idle (Cease)  last change: 00:06:40
peer 10.20.30.2   AS 65010  state: Established      last change: 00:00:15
routes received: 2k, advertised: 1.9k
```
Jonas: traffic to some onprem prefixes being blackholed via peer .1 when it withdraws. looks like the transit provider is flapping.
Maya: priority — identify customer impact list. @Evan can you run quick query for private deployments routing via westeurope-onprem links?
Evan: running. quick scan shows ~7 customers with active flows routed via the affected circuit. Top affected: AcmePayments, StudioSearch, MedForms. Error spikes in logs (502/504) line up at 1750001050.
Carol: CS is on standby; I'll open 1:1 tickets for the three named customers, advise we have a P1 and are on mitigation. ETA for first update 15m. :telephone_receiver:
Jonas: mitigation options: 1) force route failover to peer .2 by withdrawing our local routes to peer .1, 2) request transit provider to escalate the flapping session, 3) temporarily advertise prepended routes to prefer alternate path. I'm leaning to option 1 for immediate customer relief.
Maya: option 1 sounds safest — minimize config churn. @NetEng can you apply temporary withdraw to peer .1? OpsBot, schedule a config change with 5m TTL and annotate in change log.
NetEng: applying withdraw now to peer 10.20.30.1. executing change via netops automation.
OpsBot: CHANGELOG: withdraw-routes-to-peer-10.20.30.1 started by NetEng at 1750001500. runbook step: withdraw-advertisements -> verify.
NetEng: done. verified BGP adverts to .1 are down, traffic re-evaluating to peer .2.
Jonas: monitoring packet captures at edge, seeing SYNs forwarded to alt peer. initial success — error rates dropping.
Maya: app metrics show 502 spike reduced from 62% -> 12% across private routes in last 3min. still some tail errors.
Evan: logs show retries succeeding now for most customers. Recording incidents in status page: https://status.redwood.internal/incidents/1750001234
Carol: first customer updates posted to ticket for AcmePayments and StudioSearch (templates used). Customers asked for ETA and workaround (we routed them over fallback circuit).
Maya: confirmed partial recovery. Declaring mitigation in place. Next: ensure onprem circuits converge stable for 30m before opening rollback. Who will be primary for 30m watch?
Priya: I'll take watch for 30m and validate other circuits. I'll also coordinate with transit provider NOC.
Maya: handing off to @Priya at 1750001800 — details: withdraw applied to peer .1, alt peer .2 carrying traffic, monitoring dashboards: ingress/egress errors, BGP session states, application 5xx. rollback criteria: 30m stable BGP, error rate <3% for 10m, no new withdraws.
Priya: ack. joining call with provider NOC now — logs indicate upstream flapping due to maintenance misconfig on their router (they reported multi-vendor FRR issue). Provider says they will patch and hold session.
NetEng: provider asked to keep session dampening for 15m. we requested manual hold.
Jonas: note — we recorded the temporary withdraw as a config note in netops. If provider confirms fix, sequence for rollback: 1) re-advertise to peer .1 at low priority, 2) watch for route acceptance and no withdraws for 10m, 3) gradually remove prepends if any.
Maya: status update to execs and SRE team: mitigation applied, majority traffic rerouted, customers notified. P1 -> partial mitigation.
Evan: monitoring alert cleared for high-err-rate rule at 1750002100. still seeing occasional 5xx < 5%.
Carol: customers acknowledged and appreciate the proactive comms. one support escalation open for a custom VPN at AcmePayments; handing to Solutions Eng.
Priya: provider confirms patch rolled at 1750002400 and BGP session stable. requesting we re-advertise to peer .1 for recovery test.
Jonas: prepping re-advertise now. will bring adverts back at 1750002550 with per-prefix dampening off for 10m to avoid immediate withdraws.
NetEng: re-advertise complete. peer .1 state: Established. routes accepted.
Maya: metrics show traffic gradually moving back to normal paths. error rate now 1.6% and trending down.
OpsBot: INCIDENT MITIGATION: routes re-advertised to peer .1 at 1750002580 — change logged.
Priya: continuing watch for 30m after re-advertise. I'll validate BGP stability and customer health.
Maya: prepping initial post-incident summary and timeline. Postmortem meeting scheduled: 1750007200 (2h) to cover root cause, provider SLA gaps, and runbook improvements.
Jonas: root cause candidate: transit provider FRRouting bug triggered by scheduled maintenance; our automation didn't detect repeated withdraws early enough — we'll add an automated failover threshold to netops.
Maya: handoff summary to SRE oncall @Priya at 1750003000 — actions carried: withdraw to peer .1, customer comms opened, mitigation validated, rollback executed after provider patch. Next steps: postmortem, change to netops failover threshold, update runbook, reach out to provider for RCA and credits if warranted.
Priya: ack. I'll own postmortem writeup and follow up with provider. closing active paging but leaving incident open until postmortem.
Maya: thanks all. switching channel to postmortem drafting — will link notes here when ready. :white_check_mark:
